newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end lower as profit-taking hits gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end lower as profit-taking hits gains.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed slightly lower on Thursday as profit-taking emerged near the end of the session to erase gains brought on by a pension fund shopping spree, brokers said.
The spree at one point lifted the Nikkei 225 average near the 19,000 barrier, but it ended down 37.40 points or 0.20 percent at 18,698.07. Its June futures slipped 70 points to 18,700.

"Pension funds were expected to buy bellwether issues again today and they did," said Noboru Yorita, Tachibana Securities general manager. "There is likely to be more of that type of buying and the market is well-supported by the hopes."
